Go exposes FollowedByMax(maximum, tag, predicate) and FollowedByMaxExpr(expression, tag, predicate) as chainable edge-scoped operators. Runtime capacity counts only active sequence branches waiting on that edge, so nested followed-by operators release and reuse capacity independently; static and resolved dynamic maxima must be positive, and Java-invalid event-field/tag maximum expressions are rejected at Build. PatternSubexpressionLimitListener reports rejected branches after the Engine lock is released with deployment, statement, canonical edge, resolved maximum and attempted count, coalescing duplicate rejections for one input transition. Context start and per-partition end patterns additionally report context name, lifecycle phase and partition identity without merging independent partitions. Java additionally exposes runtime-URI/factory-oriented static ConditionHandler hooks and a broader engine-wide subexpression accounting surface; those remain open.

Go exposes query-level DiscardPartialsOnMatch and SuppressOverlappingMatches options for fluent Pattern queries, rejects them for non-pattern/context/join/action shapes, clears active branches after a visible completion, and suppresses overlapping captured-event results within the current result batch while allowing reuse in a later batch; policy flags also participate in Plan hash/canonical identity. Java additionally covers event-level @consume(N), every/and/or/match-until/guard/observer combinations, ordering and repeated-tag cardinality; those remain open.

Go exposes variadic Consume(level) on the fluent PatternStream (no argument means level 0) and, when one or more consuming filters match an input Event, dispatches only consuming filters at the maximum level; unannotated filters proceed only when no consuming filter matches. Followed-by, and, or, Context, filter-scene lifecycle, level zero, mixed unannotated filters, multi-branch cardinality, negative level and argument arity are covered. Java SODA rendering, exact parser diagnostics, repeated-tag cardinality and broader nested trace parity remain open.

Go TimerCron now shares opt-in second/millisecond/microsecond precision and typed special calendar operators/timezone resolution with OutputAt, TimerAtSchedule resolves the next wildcard/range/step calendar occurrence once for ordinary Pattern and Pattern Context, and TimerScheduleWithPeriod/TimerScheduleISO cover typed calendar/fixed periods, finite/unlimited recurrence, past-date anchoring, ISO date/period forms, and captured-tag ISO expressions for ordinary Pattern and recurring Pattern Context. Java SODA rendering, dynamic special-operator expressions, timezone invalid diagnostics, DST gap/overlap policy, and full nested observer trace parity remain open.

Go now covers database/sql prepared arguments, explicit typed ParameterTypes declarations for opaque SQL argument functions, byte/numeric/bool/null coercion, multi-row result snapshots, argument-keyed LRU/expiry cache with defensive result copies, result-column case normalization, caller-provided placeholder rewriting, preset question/$n/:n/@pn dialect rewriters with literal/comment/quoted-identifier scanning, column and whole-row conversion hooks (including null-row filtering), an explicit sample-metadata statement equivalent to Java metadatasql, optional PreparedStatement Close for both live and metadata statements, caller-owned transaction queryers, typed Struct/JSON/ObjectArray/Avro row materialization through the common representation boundary, a parameterized SQL Sink with new/old ordering and basic MySQL Upsert-table writes, and opt-in real MySQL Docker tests. Go also adds fluent FromMethod/FromMethodOn and DependingOn with MethodProvider/MethodProviderFunc, typed Event-returning providers, generic declared-value/single-value/iter.Seq adapters, trigger filtering, variable/parameter/dependency snapshots, statement/deployment/source/context-partition invocation metadata, stable topological polling for declaration-order-independent subordinate chains, row-identity lineage that prevents false Cartesian products, two-stream and left-deep mixed-edge N-stream outer dependency behavior through JoinChain, independent and dependency-aware historical/method multi-source FAF snapshots with source filters/windows and lineage, segmented Context FAF partitioning, plus CachedMethodProvider with explicit key functions, LRU/expiry policies and defensive Event copies. Java's EPLDatabaseFAFInvalid rejects joins between SQL result sets and Context SQL FAF; Go's typed historical/method FAF joins are an explicit extension and are not claimed as shared Java trace parity. Java's EPLDatabaseFAFPrepareExecutePerformance remains a bounded reuse check rather than a 1000-iteration timing contract; SODA is represented by immutable Go Plan construction; Java's exact invalid SQL diagnostic, full SQL type-code/dialect binding, connection pool semantics, transactional/retry connector behavior, remaining mixed-edge permutations/performance, context lifecycle/UDF/script combinations, invalid parity and full trace remain open.

Go's fluent builder rejects duplicate definitions/operators/routes, unknown operators and ports, incompatible typed edges, undeclared schemas, ordinary cycles, source-targeted input edges, non-cyclic feedback markers, non-canonical names/ports and terminal-sink output edges; the feedback bit also participates in Plan canonical/hash identity. EPL parser syntax, Java forge/class resolution, annotation property injection and reflective onInput method discovery have no runtime analogue in the typed Go API: Go factories, port descriptors and Process/Run interfaces make those shapes compile-time contracts instead.

Go adds fluent EmitterPorts and uses stable named SubmitPort routing instead of Java's numeric port index. Captive handles expose their stable definition name, ambiguous Submit is rejected for multiple outputs, a single named output remains usable through Submit, and SubmitSignal fans out once over every connected output for both captive Emitter and custom-source handles. Declared port names and Go types participate in Plan canonical/hash identity; Java's exact numeric-index exception text and reflection-based stream schemas are intentionally replaced by named fluent descriptors.

Go adds the fluent EventBusSourceWithFilter and EventBusSourceWithUnderlying APIs: filters evaluate against the Event envelope, while accepted values can enter graph or linear paths as the raw registered Go value. Struct, Map, ObjectArray and XML source representations are now exercised through the same typed graph boundary. Java additionally covers EventBean/object-array collector modes and broader source parameter/representation diagnostics; those remain open.

Go adds fluent EventBusSourceWithCollector and EventBusSinkWithCollector callbacks. Source collectors may suppress, duplicate or transform incoming typed events and may return Event envelopes or registered Go values; sink collectors return zero or more explicit event-type/value emissions, including dynamic target types, while preserving variant envelopes. Static EventBusSink now also materializes native Struct, Map, ObjectArray and XML values, matching Java's Beacon/source-to-sink representation boundary. Java's EventBean/object-array collector context APIs, Beacon-driven collector setup and exact collector diagnostics remain open.

Go adds terminal LogSinkWithOptions with summary/json/xml rendering, event and projection-row shapes, layout placeholders (%df/%p/%i/%t/%e), title, linefeed control and an injectable writer callback; the legacy LogSink callback remains available. LogSink output edges are rejected like Java. Java additionally selects SLF4J versus stdout through its log flag, evaluates EPL parameters at instantiation, uses Java EventBean summary/toString rules and covers a broader renderer/property matrix; Go uses typed options and Go writer semantics instead.

Go exposes public FinalMarker, WindowMarker and CustomSignal values, OnSignal handlers, graph propagation and terminal Emitter observation. DataflowInstance.StartCaptive opens operator/source lifecycle once and returns a DataflowCaptive containing a defensive named-emitter map plus definition-ordered, single-use Beacon/custom-source runnables; sources are never launched automatically and their normal return leaves the instance Running until explicit Cancel, matching Java EPDataFlowInstanceCaptive. Each runnable supports synchronous Run, asynchronous Start, Wait/Done, source-only idempotent Shutdown, IsShutdown and completion listeners carrying name/error/canceled state; late listeners receive the retained completion immediately, and instance cancellation propagates to running sources. Captive emitter Submit/SubmitSignal remains usable after a final marker, while instance cancellation closes runtimes and invalidates submission. Java additionally exposes next()-level stepping/audit hooks; typed EventBean/object-array coercion, persisted saved instances, concurrent signal delivery and broader exception recovery remain open.

Go covers contiguous sequence/alternation/finite permutation/repetition including bounded and unbounded nested groups, reluctant quantifiers, partition, fixed/calendar interval completion, basic interval-or-terminated lifecycle, measure-alias order-by, current-window Prev in DEFINE, typed tag-aware PrevTag/PriorTag field references in DEFINE and MEASURES, statement snapshot, length-window eviction and Named Window out-of-sequence deletion/recomputation with field-based measure aggregation; Java calendar/termination matrix, full after/iterator/order-by, advanced NFA forms, advanced tag-aware previous-reference variants, advanced aggregation and full trace equality remain open.

Go covers length-window eviction, time-window expiry/iterator recomputation, time-batch pending iterator state and boundary reset, named-window consumer deployment replay from retained state, the unbound-stream contract that listener matches are delivered while Statement.Snapshot is empty, and Named Window deletion/recomputation. TestRowRecogNamedWindowDeleteOutOfSequencePrev, TestRowRecogNamedWindowDeleteOutOfSequence and TestRowRecogNamedWindowDeleteInSequence map Java RowRecogDelete's PREV-referenced, out-of-sequence and in-sequence delete executions, including partial-match removal, arrival-order PREV retention, repeated captures and Snapshot/listener results. TestRowRecogIterateOnlyNoListenerMode, TestRowRecogIterateOnlyPrev and TestRowRecogIterateOnlyPrevPartitioned map Java RowRecogIterateOnly's window/PREV/partitioned iterator behavior: arrivals update retention and previous-access history without NFA/listener output, while Snapshot recomputes the current match; IterateOnly also avoids consuming the MatchRecognize state pool. Full OOSD repository ordering, delete/update interaction, context-owned named-window replay and complete Java output trace still require parity work.

Both Java RowRecogDataSet executions are now mapped: TestRowRecogDataSetFinancialPattern covers A B C* D E* F+ and E7/E8/E9 batches, while TestRowRecogFinancialWPatternDataSet covers the 60-event A W+ X+ Y+ Z+ unbound financial trace and all terminal batches. TestRowRecogPartitionMultikeyWithArrayContent maps Java RowRecogMultikeyWArray's array-content partition identity, including nil and empty arrays, while TestRowRecogPartitionMultikeyPlainTuple maps the int/long composite partition tuple. The RowRecogAfter matrix is now covered by TestRowRecogAfterCurrentRowKeepsTheRecognizingBranch, TestRowRecogAfterNextRowContinuation, TestRowRecogAfterSkipToNextRowDataSet, TestRowRecogAfterSkipToNextRowRepeatedVariable, TestRowRecogAfterSkipToNextRowPartitioned, and TestRowRecogAfterSkipPastLastRow; the last case also fixes Snapshot retention of already-emitted rows while excluding skip-pruned future starts. The four Java RowRecogInterval executions are now mapped by TestRowRecogIntervalSimpleTrace, TestRowRecogIntervalPartitionedTrace, TestRowRecogIntervalMultipleCompletedTrace, and TestRowRecogIntervalMonthScopedTrace, covering pending Snapshot rows, absolute deadline listener batches, partition-local deadlines, multiple completed starts, and calendar month boundaries. TestRowRecogIntervalResolutionExactBoundary and TestRowRecogIntervalResolutionMicrosecondBoundary map the A* pending/exact flip behavior and the Java WConfig 10,000,000-microsecond boundary through Go's explicit time.Duration/time.Time model, including listener and Snapshot. TestRowRecogRegexMatrix maps all 12 Java RowRecogRegex pattern holders with chainable optional, alternation, nested/repeated group and repeated-capture patterns, comparing both listener output and Statement.Snapshot output. TestRowRecogVariantStreamPreservesMemberType maps the Java PREDEFINED variant A/B member-type scenario through typed InsertInto routes and concrete Event.TypeName predicates; invalid member/source/direct-payload routes are covered separately. The same inventory adds an engine-wide MaxStates/PreventStart policy with immutable overflow events, per-statement counts, cross-statement/context/named-window lifecycle tests and undeploy release coverage, plus time-window expiry, time-batch pending/boundary iterator tests from RowRecogDataWin, the unbound-stream listener/empty-Snapshot contract, partition-local rolling PREV history that remains usable after time-window eviction, and RowRecogIterateOnly's window/PREV/partitioned Snapshot recomputation without listener output. The ten Java RowRecogIntervalOrTerminated execution methods are now mapped by chainable listener/Snapshot tests covering mismatch termination, finite terminals, timer continuation, ALL MATCHES and alternation/repeated-group branches. Java TestSuiteRowRecog ran 23/23 and TestSuiteRowRecogWConfig ran 4/4 in selected Maven runs. Exact Java NFA state counts for nested/repeated transitions, Java global TimeSource time-unit configuration surface, remaining complex/calendar IntervalOrTerminated combinations, full Variant/ANY/dynamic-member trace, iterate-only performance baseline, advanced tag-aware PRIOR/PREV variants, invalid diagnostics and ordering behavior remain open.

Go now compares the runtime-wide state-pool successor counts for optional bypasses (A? B? C), permuted repeated branches (permute(A,B)* C), nested repeated groups ((A B)* C), and Java finite range expansion (A{2,3} B). The assertions follow Java RowRecogNFAView.step: consume each current state, charge every successor before the next event evaluates it, and release terminal successors. Full Java plan introspection, dynamic quantifiers, branch ordering and all interval/termination compositions remain open.

Go covers a bounded high-partition lifecycle trace with chainable PartitionBy/AllMatches, completed A-B pairs, and a second wave of pending A states followed by partition-local B completion. The Java stress cardinality and runtime-specific partition repository thresholds still require a dedicated performance/reclamation harness.

Go provides a fixed-worker FIFO queue, same-thread fallback, named ExecutorServices registry, structured unknown/closed errors, graceful drain, context cancellation, panic conversion, observable Task.Wait errors, async DML/Upsert retry and lifecycle re-check before SQL execution. Java's RunnableDML/RunnableUpsert log and swallow final failures, while Go deliberately exposes them through Task.Wait; Java JNDI binding, XML configuration population, per-event connection factory acquisition and exact logging/diagnostic text remain open.

Go covers a standard-library HTTP client sink with sorted query encoding, stream/property URI templates, JSON request bodies, bounded responses, retry and lifecycle, plus an HTTP server source with method/path/query/header/body capture, pause/stop/restart and an Engine bridge. The pinned Java esperio-http module ran 4 tests: 3 passed and TestHTTPAdapterOutput failed in the current environment due to the legacy subscription/URI compile and connection setup path. Java XML configuration, classic HTTP service handler behavior, async delivery, response/error mapping and full shared trace remain open.

Go covers a concurrent TCP source with key/value CSV, property-ordered CSV, stream-prefixed JSON, Java escape decoding, typed Engine record materialization, multiple clients, pause/resume, stop/restart and a registered object decoder. XML configuration/plugin loading, writable-property cache parity, backlog/host binding details, full malformed-input diagnostics and shared Java/Go trace remain open.

Go provides a provider-neutral process-outside bridge contract for Map/Text/Object/Bytes messages, Java InputAdapter event-type property names, DecodeAny/JSON/Object hooks, acknowledge-after-process, retry, pause/resume, factory restart, Engine bridge and deterministic Map/Text output. The Java esperio-springjms module ran 4 tests with 1 pass and 3 failures in the current ActiveMQ/JMX and message-type-marker environment. JVM JMS provider/session/transaction semantics, Spring XML context/plugin loading, listener container recovery and Java Serializable compatibility remain open.

Go covers a RabbitMQ amqp091-go Consumer/Publisher bridge, Java-style host/port/user/vhost and queue/exchange declaration, generated queues, prefetch, JSON/GOB codec hooks, Engine bridge, auto-ack or manual ack-after-process/immediate modes, reject/requeue, retry, pause/resume, factory restart, ordered JSON sink output and real RabbitMQ source/sink round-trips. Java Serializable wire compatibility, Dataflow graph/operator registration, reconnect/connection recovery and shared Java/Go trace remain open.

Go covers a kafka-go-backed Reader/Writer bridge, injected reader/writer contracts, JSON processor, Engine map/struct bridge, commit-after-processing, immediate commit mode, retry, timestamp hook, source factory restart, producer JSON encoding with ordered schema fields, keys/headers and lifecycle. An initial no-broker/no-topic run is retained as an external environment diagnostic, not a semantic failure. Consumer group/rebalance/offset recovery, custom Java serializer/deserializer loading, annotated-statement plugin registration, advanced broker recovery and full shared trace remain open.

Go implements the equality/hash shared-index subset plus automatic equality-prefix + range B-tree shared indexes with a fluent NamedWindowSubqueryIndexSharing option, automatic internal index creation and reuse, explicit SubqueryUseIndex, consumer-side SubqueryDisableIndexSharing, SubqueryNoIndex, Build-time invalid-option diagnostics and index rebuild after insert/update/delete for global and Context-partitioned Named Windows. Go provides typed MethodProvider/MethodProviderFunc and FromMethodOn/FromMethod builders instead of Java reflection-based static method invocation. The mapped slice covers no-argument array/object returns, method result returned as Map/POJO/ObjectArray, overloaded parameter dispatch by the provider, basic invalid-build checks for unknown trigger stream and nil provider, N-stream method-historical joins with star-subordinate CartesianLast, forward/chain subordinate and joined-keepall semantics, 2-stream/3-stream alias-driven subordinate lookups, variable-driven 3-historical pure/no-subordinate, 1-subordinate and chained-subordinate snapshots, named-window-twice aliased method joins (Stream.As logical source aliases), and outer N-stream joins: inner/left/right/full chained variants of the 1-stream-2-hist and 2-stream-1-hist subordinate matrices, evaluate-once constant-argument method streams (Stream.EvaluateOnce) seeded once at deployment with outer placeholders visible to the iterator, unsatisfiable outer-dependency build diagnostics, and the outer forward matrices: 1-stream-2-hist/1-stream-3-hist #lastevent forward subordinate left-outer chains, the mixed right/left/full 3-hist variant run as declared, and the chained-prefix 3-hist variant (fetchVal(s0.id||-H0)/fetchVal(h0.val||-H1)/fetchVal(h1.val||-H2)). Java NoSubordinate second textual variant (h1 left outer join s0 right outer join h0) asserts the identical tryAssertionSeven matrix in Java and is modeled through the observably equivalent s0-anchored right-outer chain. Cache LRU/expiry, context bindings, multikey/array-key joins, join performance and full Java method footprint/return-type diagnostics remain open.
